distinguishing_features: Passive static flow-geometry modification (baffles) vs. active procedure changes (VFD modulation, parameter reduction, pulsed recirculation)
No moving parts or external power vs. active agitation or thermal control
Directly targets Stokes' law settling via inertial recirculation vs. indirect approaches (shear modulation, Weber number reduction, thermal shock)
Drop-in hardware solution vs. process parameter adjustments
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Maintaining slurry particle suspension homogeneity in delivery lines to prevent settling-induced wafer removal drift without adding moving parts or external energy
parsed.viable_reason: The static baffle design leverages existing hydraulic energy and fluid dynamics principles (Dean vortices, critical shear velocity) to maintain suspension, with calculations showing local velocities far exceed Stokes' settling threshold.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior arts focus on active modulation (VFD, parameter changes) or post-failure mitigation, whereas the passive flow-geometry approach with inertial recirculation represents a novel mechanism class not suggested by existing solutions.
